Meta.title: Dataset Doctor — Understand your dataset before training
Meta.description: Dataset Doctor surfaces missing values, duplicates, class imbalance, suspicious features and leakage in a clear diagnostic report — before you train your model.

Hero.title:
Know your dataset

before you train

your model.
Hero.ledeLead: Catch data quality problems before they become model problems.
Hero.ledeRest: Dataset Doctor helps surface missing values, duplicates, imbalance, suspicious features and other common dataset issues in a clear report.
Hero.conceptNote: A design concept — an open-source Python toolkit in the making. Every figure here is illustrative.

Problem.title: Model problems often begin before training starts.
Problem.body: Most teams discover dataset problems too late — after hours spent tuning architectures and hyperparameters that were never the bottleneck. By then the fix belongs upstream, and the experiments have to be re-run.
Problem.quote: A model trained on a sick dataset learns the sickness.

symptoms.name: Data leakage
symptoms.gloss: Answer keys in the training frame

Features.title:
Everything worth checking

before model.fit()
Features.body: Eight passes over the schema, the statistics and the relationships between them — the quiet checks that decide whether a model will generalize.

big1.label: Pass 01 · Completeness
big1.title: Missing Value Analysis
big1.body: Null patterns grouped by column, dtype and row segment — not just one sad total count.
big1.caption: Filled squares mark present values, red outlines mark nulls — 4 of 31 columns carry nulls · 0.8% of cells

big2.label: Pass 02 · Uniqueness
big2.title: Duplicate Detection
big2.body: Exact and near-duplicate rows caught by fingerprint hashing, across every column pair.
big2.caption: Row bars preview record fingerprints; matching rows highlight amber — 218 rows collapse into 109 unique records

compact.label: Pass 03
compact.title: Class Distribution
compact.body: Majority and minority priors, surfaced before they skew metrics.

compact.label: Pass 04
compact.title: Outlier Detection
compact.body: Values drifting far outside their column's expected range.

compact.label: Pass 05
compact.title: Data Type Validation
compact.body: Numerics stored as strings, dates stored as anything but.

compact.label: Pass 06
compact.title: Leakage Warnings
compact.body: Features holding answers they should not have access to.

corr.label: Pass 07 · Relationships
corr.title: Correlation Analysis
corr.body: Which features move together — and which ones happen to move with the target.
corr.note: Example finding: field_12 and field_27 have<hi> ρ 0.94</hi> — review for leakage

summary.label: Overview
summary.title: Dataset Summary
summary.body: The factual shape of your data, before any modelling decision.

Health.title: One score. A clearer starting point.
Health.body: Dataset Health summarizes common quality signals to help identify which areas deserve attention before training.
Health.disclaimer: <lbl>Concept preview</lbl> — this page is a product concept. Scores and findings shown here are illustrative, not computed from real data.

Report.title: Problems, prioritized.
Report.body: Every finding ships with evidence and a suggested next action — sorted by severity, so the first hour goes to the biggest risk.
Report.excerptNote: Selected findings — the full report lists every check with its evidence.

findings.title: Potential target leakage
findings.body: The feature "customer_status" has a suspiciously strong relationship with the target.
findings.action: Review whether this column would actually be available at prediction time.

findings.title: Class imbalance detected
findings.body: Training on this split will bias the model toward the majority class unless it is weighted or resampled.
findings.action: Weight the classes or resample the training split before fitting; report precision and recall per class instead of plain accuracy.

findings.title: Duplicate observations
findings.action: Keep one copy of each duplicated record and regenerate the split before training — or trace why duplicates enter the pipeline upstream.

in three steps.

Dev.title: Fits into the workflow you already use.
Dev.body: Run one command in CI, or import the analyzer beside your notebook. Either way the report arrives as a single self-contained HTML file.
Dev.apiNote: Command and API shown are illustrative — the interface is still being shaped.

OSS.title: Transparent by design.
OSS.body: Dataset Doctor is envisioned as an open-source toolkit that developers can inspect, extend and integrate into their existing workflows.

pillars.title: Open Source
pillars.body: Read every check, audit every heuristic, ship your own fork.

pillars.title: Python First
pillars.body: A proposed interface for notebooks, scripts and pipelines.

pillars.title: Extensible Checks
pillars.body: A proposed catalogue of checks with room for custom validation passes.

CTA.sub: Catch obvious dataset problems before spending time optimizing the wrong model.
